questions.q: What is the author's main message?
options: Anyone can train their mind to concentrate through daily practice
Reading should be done only in the evening before bed
Commuting is the best time to read an encyclopaedia for learning
Physical exercise matters more than training the mind each morning
questions.explain: He says mind control is possible by persevering in concentration, which cures worry.

questions.q: When does the author suggest practicing concentration?
options: During the evening hour before you go to bed
On the way from your door to your office
In the quiet minutes just after lunch at work
At weekends in a quiet room with a good book
questions.explain: He reserves the time from leaving your door to arriving at your office.

questions.q: Roughly how many times will you bring your mind back before reaching the station?
options: About four
About fourteen
About forty
About four hundred
questions.explain: Ere you reach the station you will have brought it back about forty times.

questions.q: Whose writings does the author suggest concentrating on?
options: Plato and Socrates
Shakespeare and Milton
Homer and Virgil
Marcus Aurelius or Epictetus
questions.explain: He suggests a little chapter of Marcus Aurelius or Epictetus.

questions.q: Why does the author recall the morning of the disquieting letter?
options: To show the mind can concentrate when sufficiently roused
To show that letters of reply should be written at home
To warn that anxiety ruins any attempt at concentration
To argue that trains are the worst place for thinking
questions.explain: That case shows you can dominate your mind like a tyrant, so lack of concentration is not incapacity.
